title: Channel Visual Identity Specification
description: Addendum section 2. One entry per channel, keyed by channel_id, in config/visual-identity.json. Every field is REQUIRED and every enum is closed: the point of this file is that a channel's visual world is DECLARED, not inferred at render time. Section 2 forbids automated generation of these values -- they are curated by a human from the Style Reference Document produced by the section-1 research phase, and `human_validated` records that step. Nothing may reach a production render without it.

channels.description: channel_id -> specification. A channel absent from here has no visual identity and, per section 3, its render must abort rather than fall back.

hex.description: Six-digit hex. Colour lives in config, never in a prompt-generated string (CHECK-REGISTER SCR-13).

primary_palette.description: Exactly 4, ordered most to least prominent.

typography_primary.description: Font family name. The validator checks it against the woff2 files actually present in src/skills/remotion-render/public/fonts -- section 2 requires the font be available in the rendering environment, and a name that is not there is a render-time failure, not a preference.

core_objects.description: At least 5 specific object types that define this channel's visual world. Section 8 makes this list load-bearing: a chart type may only be drawn if it is named here.

camera_language.description: At least 4 permitted moves, ordered by preference. Any move NOT listed is forbidden for this channel.

transition_language.description: Exactly 3, ordered by frequency of use.

use_of_negative_space.description: high = more than 60% empty, medium = 40-60%, low = less than 40%.

style_reference_document.description: Repo-relative path to the immutable Style Reference Document (section 1.5) this specification was curated from. The validator requires the file to exist: a specification with no research behind it is exactly what section 1 exists to prevent.

human_validated.description: Section 2: 'must be validated by a human before it is used in any production render'. This block is the only machine-readable record of that, so the gate can refuse an unvalidated specification instead of trusting a convention. NOTE FOR REVIEW: section 2 mandates the human validation but does not specify how it is recorded -- this block is the minimum mechanism to enforce what section 2 requires, and is the one field here not named verbatim in the addendum.
